intent_snapshot.goal: Make the scheduler's scope-overlap check and ready buffer use work item facts, emit E2 only on Issue body or title change, and include head_sha in E8 event identity, per D7 of docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md. No user-visible change: scheduling internals.

acceptance.assertion: Source BR-GAP-2, BR-GAP-3; meet D7 in docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-sched-scheduler.test.ts over scheduleLoopWork fed from dispatch. Done looks like: two candidates whose work item scopes overlap run one and hold the other, and ready_buffer equals the number of work items in plan_published. Negative: disjoint scopes both run. Bound: reaching max_ready_buffer holds further planning candidates.

Source BR-GAP-6, BR-GAP-7; meet D7 in docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-sched-scheduler.test.ts and tests/loop-daemon-observe.test.ts, characterization first for E2. Done looks like: an Issue body edit emits E2 and two failures of one check on different heads get different E8 event_id values. Negative: a comment-only update that changes updated_at emits no E2. Bound: the same head and failure signature share one event_id.

attestations.summary: Provenance verified: the commit's only parent is the base and the tree is 0e64e77. The scheduler now builds each candidate's scope from its work item's bound TaskIntents or published plan; an empty scope still overlaps every lease through scopesOverlap. ready_buffer now counts plan_published work items. E2 fires only when the stored title+body hash changes, and the E8 event_id now carries head_sha. Tests cover overlap, disjoint scopes, the buffer bound and the E2/E8 identity cases. Blast radius: medium, in loop_daemon dispatch.ts, events.ts, observer.ts and work_items.ts, plus the persisted issue-content keys in etag_by_resource. The antigravity mirrors are byte-identical to the main plugin files.

advisory_findings.summary: The tests rebuild the candidate with the helpers dispatch uses, but they never call dispatchDecisions, so the two dispatch wiring lines (scope_hint from workItemScopeHint, ready_buffer from plannedWorkItemCount) have no test at the 'fed from dispatch' seam.

evidence.trigger: If someone reverts dispatch.ts to read scope_hint from the event or sets ready_buffer back to 0, tests/loop-sched-scheduler.test.ts still passes because it calls scheduleLoopWork directly.

advisory_findings.summary: workItemScopeHint silently drops a bound task whose intent fails to read, so a partly readable binding gives a smaller non-empty scope instead of the empty scope that serializes the work.

evidence.trigger: A work item is bound to tasks [a, b] and b's intent sidecar is unreadable, so the scope is only a's scope_hint and a candidate that overlaps only b's paths is dispatched at the same time.
